answer: Identity is a scarce, taxed seat, not a free key. A fixed board of seats is auctioned; each holder self-assesses its seat's worth, pays a recurring tax on that figure, and anyone may buy the seat at the stated price. A sybil farm must hold many seats, so it pays tax on every clone forever and watches honest buyers pick off its weakest ones. An alias may publish its own sonnet, yet the rent still falls due; a prism can split one owner into many colors, but each color owes the same fee, and the buyout signal stays loud. Cost tracks live identities and exposed capital, not registration.
